name: BEAM (carmustine/etoposide/cytarabine/melphalan) conditioning for autologous transplant

institution.provenance: DRAFT decision-support protocol authored from standard-of-care knowledge (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison, general reference); experimental, not clinically activated

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: high-emetogenic multi-day conditioning; use a guideline-based multi-drug regimen

premedications.name: Seizure/pulmonary precautions
premedications.notes: carmustine can cause pneumonitis and infusional hypotension; infuse slowly

supportiveCare: Delivered as a single high-dose conditioning course immediately before autologous stem-cell reinfusion (conventionally days -6 to -1)
Full transplant supportive care: broad antimicrobial prophylaxis, transfusion support, mucositis care, and G-CSF per unit protocol
Cryopreserved autologous stem cells reinfused after melphalan clears
monitoring: Daily CBC and organ function through the aplastic period
This is myeloablative - only give where stem-cell rescue is available

drugs.name: Carmustine (BCNU)
drugs.notes: 300 mg/m2 IV on day 1 (conventionally day -6). Slow infusion; monitor for hypotension and delayed pneumonitis.

drugs.name: Etoposide
drugs.notes: 200 mg/m2 per day IV, days 2-5 (often split as 100 mg/m2 every 12 h).

drugs.name: Cytarabine
drugs.notes: 400 mg/m2 per day IV, days 2-5 (200 mg/m2 every 12 h).

drugs.name: Melphalan
drugs.notes: 140 mg/m2 IV on day 6 (day -1); ice-chip cryotherapy to reduce mucositis. Autologous cells reinfused after clearance.
